reason: A explains the system more clearly to a newcomer: a short overview splits the work between the admin's request and the background jobs, one named function (applyRefundTransition) makes every status change, and claims stop two workers calling the provider at once, while B spreads the transition logic over several steps that partly overlap and leaves gaps such as step 5b's vague check of "whether an earlier attempt may have created it."

author: haiku
reason: B says at the start which parts run in the admin's request and which run in background jobs. It sends every status change through one named transition function and uses an explicit claim so two callers never call the provider at once, which makes the system easier to understand as a whole. A is linear and readable, but it leaves key mechanics vague, such as how step 5b "checks whether an earlier attempt may have created it", and it leaves a 4xx write failure unhandled.
